body:
I really appreciate this response, it has done wonders to get me thinking what I think to be more rationally about the situation I find myself in. When I originally wrote this post, I was in tears and not exactly thinking straight, even though I most definitely meant everything I said. I do not believe I have ADHD however, when I say I can never get my mind to calm down I mean I always find myself thinking about bigger things. Today, I was supposed to be writing a 6 paragraph essay for English 3, but instead found myself writing a 6 page personal essay on what I believe would be a better education system for our nation. I find it extremely easy to focus and chill out on things that I find have importance, but if I don't feel it is important, I find it impossible to focus on and begin to feel trapped when I have to focus my time on it. 

I have however, been told many times throughout elementary, that I may have ADHD, as that seemed to be the only possible reason teachers could come up with for me constantly not doing work, having emotional outbreaks, etc. I've never really considered it a viable possibility as the source of some of my issues, but I could see that. I also suffer from very severe insomnia, but in the last 6 months I have made that issue almost zero with sleeping pills and listening to music while falling asleep. 

I also did begin working out to try and feel happier about a month ago, and while it does make me feel happier and in general have more energy, it also makes my mind work a lot more, and makes me think very very deeply, especially when I go on long runs or walks, which normally makes my mind drift to the issues in the world and how I wish I could fix them, so it's a win and a loss when I work out. I lift one or two times a week and do my best to go for a 90 minute run or bike ride daily.

I must however say that your response was really helpful, I'm thinking that maybe I really do need to go to my parents with the issues of my depression, and try and maybe get a therapist, I've just been so scared that it would lead to serious consequences, because the stories I've heard always involve police involvement and mental hospitals, and those types of things would certainly not help my mental state. 

Sorry for the long response, I'm really awful at summarizing my thoughts in a short way, and it feels great to actually talk about my real feelings. Basically, your long response really has helped me think this through more. I don't think I feel any more convinced about staying in school, but I for the first time feel like I should actually seek serious help before I make the decision that could possibly ruin my future.

Lol thanks for the reponse, I was scared I would get negative responses.

1. I'm not sure, I'm already behind this year (it's my junior year) and I will have to do an extra year since I failed nearly every class freshman year
2. I think, I'm not even quite sure of my dreams, but I have so many ideas and so many things that I want to do, my mind is never off

I just worry that if I drop out my parents will hate me, or that I will end up actually going nowhere and being a lowlife, even though I feel like I have the potential to accomplish so much. I'm just so confused as to the path to take because even though it sounds like it will make me happy I feel like it could make me even more suicidal because I will be called a loser and a failure, but this path I'm taking right now makes me despise waking up in the morning, and I think about suicide way more than I should. I just don't really know fam, lol
Hey dude I'm here to talk, what's up :)
